Sen2Cor had the second-lowest inland median spectral angle, ahead of Acolite. Across all datasets Sen2Cor and l2gen performed worst. Versions: Sen2Cor v2.4.0, Acolite v20170718.

evidence.locator: Abstract

evidence.locator: Section 3.1 Atmospheric correction processors

evidence.locator: Section 5 Conclusions

evidence.quote: Acolite attained higher R2 in the red and NIR bands
evidence.locator: Section 4.5. Not in W5 or W6, but it bears on how to read them

Table A3 inland statistics, page 285. Columns are N, R2, RMSD. Read from the full table: ACOLITE RMSD is lower than Sen2Cor's at 443, 490, 665, 705, and 740 nm and higher at 560, 782, and 865 nm. Sen2Cor's first row is 'Sen2Cor 443 160 0.46 0.0042'

verdicts.reason: Every element of W5 and W6 matches the paper, including the processor versions, the second-place spectral angle for Sen2Cor ahead of Acolite, and the all-datasets result. The 'second-lowest' rank holds for median spectral angle only. In Table A3 the older Acolite (SWIR-NIR aerosol, not dark spectrum fitting) has lower inland RMSD than Sen2Cor in five of eight bands, so the metric chosen decides the order.
verdicts.suggested_correction: None needed. Optionally add to W6: 'By RMSD, Acolite was lower than Sen2Cor at five of eight inland bands (Table A3).' That makes the metric dependence visible.

verdicts.reason: The conclusion holds for the ACOLITE part. These studies and four more I found do not agree on whether ACOLITE beats Sen2Cor over inland water, so decision 0008 cannot rest on a demonstrated accuracy gap. The sentence 'the four studies read disagree' is too broad, because Warren, Pereira-Sandoval, and Shan all put C2RCC (and Polymer where tested) ahead of both Sen2Cor and ACOLITE on their main metrics. The record also omits that the 2026 paper documenting the USGS product could not be read (HTTP 403), so its reported Sen2Cor comparison is unchecked.
verdicts.suggested_correction: Reword the first two bullets: 'Three of the four studies put C2RCC, and Polymer where tested, ahead of both Sen2Cor and ACOLITE on their main metrics. ACIX-Aqua did not test Sen2Cor. The studies disagree on the order of Sen2Cor and ACOLITE, and the order changes with the metric within Warren et al. and within Shan et al.' Add one sentence: 'Ducar et al. (2026), which documents the USGS product, could not be read (HTTP 403) and may contain a direct comparison. Martins et al. (2017) and Li et al. (2023) also compare Sen2Cor with ACOLITE and favor Sen2Cor in their sites.' Keep the decision 0008 paragraph.

limitations: Every quote in this file was machine-checked as a substring of text I extracted myself with pdftotext or curl (whitespace and hyphenated line breaks normalized). Two runs of the check are in the scratchpad. The Li et al. PDF has an overlapping text layer, so I quoted only passages that extracted cleanly.

Ducar et al. (2026), the paper that documents the USGS product, was not readable. Wiley returned 403 to curl and WebFetch, OpenAlex shows no repository copy, and the Chrome extension was not connected. I did not try to get around the block. V-LIT-6 is therefore incomplete on the single most relevant paper.
The Qiandao Lake paper (Allam et al. 2024) was not read. Its publisher page needs a cookie handshake and Crossref has no abstract.
Web search was used only to find candidate papers. Its summaries are not evidence, and two of them disagreed with each other about Ducar et al. I rely on none of those summaries.

The activation date of baseline 05.13 rests on one report section. I did not query the Earth Search or CDSE catalogs for 05.13 items sensed on or after 21 September 2026, because that is a provider contact outside this review.
I checked claims W1, W3, W5 to W8, R5, and the review headline only. I did not check W2, W4, or W9 to W11, and I did not re-audit the check records in water-correction-checks.json.

I could not tell from the papers whether Warren, Pereira-Sandoval, and Shan ran Sen2Cor with default or tuned settings. Only Warren (2.4.0) names a version, so none of the studies speaks for Sen2Cor 2.12, 2.13, or baseline 05.13.
WATERHYPERNET's first author belongs to the institute behind ACOLITE, and Ducar et al. include the ACOLITE developer. Neither is independent evidence for ACOLITE over Sen2Cor.
The Table A3 comparison of ACOLITE and Sen2Cor RMSD in Warren et al. is my reading of the table text from the layout extraction, not a statement of the authors.
